_why: The scripted control arm's expected metric means over the final-evaluation corpus, DECLARED so a harness regression is detectable. Without a declared baseline the lane refuses to call the model arm reportable at all — a metric that moved could not be attributed to the model rather than to the harness — so a hold-out run with no baseline can never satisfy AIC-19 however well the model does.
_measured: Read off the control arm of the committed hold-out record docs/evidence/final-evaluation/cf68c16c8592.json, over a 30-record run with no provider call. The axes do NOT all cover 30 examples: observedBaseline reports exampleCount 30 for unsupported_claim_rate and termination_correctness, 3 for false_alert_correctness, and 6 each for misleading_evidence_handling and challenge_effect, because a behaviour axis only scores the scenarios that exercise it. An earlier version of this line said all five were measured over 30 records.
_limit: Zero is the WORST score for these axes, so this baseline pins a floor. A harness change that moves a metric UP is detected; one that pushes it further down cannot be, because there is no further down. README.md states this at length.
_completeness: Every axis the control arm observes must appear here. That is enforced, not remembered: see live-model-lane.test.mjs > 'refuses a control baseline that leaves an observed axis undeclared, naming the axes and what to do'. The first version of this file declared two of the five while the lane compared two, which published a harness regression as model quality.
